title: Design Direction Change
author: 0bscuris
selftext:
One of the positives of ai game design that was not intuitive to me but has become apparent as i have playtested more and more is how much less i am stuck in bad design choices i make early on. 

The sunk cost is so much less when i can just be like, ok. This isn’t working, branch here just in case and let’s change fundamental things. 

I don’t have that sense of like, i already put 3 weeks into those code or a bunch of money into it and  i gotta make it work. 

Instead i just write a prompt, here is what i don’t like, here is why i think it is happening, here is how i want to address it, then i go have coffee.

comments.author: GCC_GicaCamelCase
comments.body: Test entire systems, not just small features. A boring/annoying small feature might make a system more complex/interesting.

comments.author: TommyGameDev
comments.body:
Yea, I feel the same, and it’s freeing to not feel so bad about throwing away something that didn’t work out. 

However, there’s two (potentially negative) factors that I’ve also felt recently. 

One is that the constant ideas and trying out new things all the time, is happening at such a fast rate now that my brain is constantly in motion, thinking about the next idea before I even evaluated the first and suddenly the review burden and context switch is stacking up.

The other is that there’re still the usage and cost, and the more things you throw at the wall to see what sticks, and with the review rounds and iterations, it makes me worried that I become too dependent on my expensive subscription, before I even see a penny of revenue.

replies.author: 0bscuris
replies.body:
The second applies less to me cuz this is just a hobby. So if I used all my credits, awesome. I’m getting my moneys worth since it’s flat fee for number of credits, but I understand what ur saying. 

Same with the first point too, so easy to start stuff it’s like ok lets do this real quick.

replies.author: TommyGameDev
replies.body: Fair. I started out like that too, but then I got too invested in the project.

comments.author: snobesque
comments.body: Same happens with all the dev process: code, graphics, etc. You either opt in or loose the competition

comments.author: UncleJoesLandscaping
comments.body: I had a few ideas that didnt work out that would have taken a week or two to do by hand. AI let me abandon the idea in an hour.

replies.author: 0bscuris
replies.body: Yeah, for sure. Knowing what ideas don’t have legs is quite a good value.

comments.author: DerekPaxton
comments.body: Yes. It is incredible for prototyping. You don’t care about sustainability or structure. You just want to get an idea in quickly to test. A ideal use case for AI.

replies.author: 0bscuris
replies.body: I did alot of game jams and the stuff that would take us 2-3 days in a team of four, i can basically do in a morning while i’m drinking my coffee. The quality isn’t great but it gets me into the core loop so fast.

comments.author: dantemp
comments.body: Yeah, which means you can be more brave with design and try more things until you get something really worth it.

replies.author: 0bscuris
replies.body:
Yeah, i mean, alot of times i come to the same conclusion thst some other game did, that i didn’t really understand why they did it. 

For example stats: i didn’t really understand why single player games had stats cuz who cares if ur op, it’s single player.

So i tried doing like a more skyrim esque leveling system and halfway through it’s like, oh i see, makes the math on the backend alot easier and groups skills together in a neat way.

comments.author: johnesco
comments.body: Sometimes I felt myself going into "most games have this, so why not mine?" a lot of driving games have a "near miss" bonus. But I added it, and caught myself /trying/ to get it by glancing cars. Changed the whole feel but in a bad way. Backed up and made a change, there was a natural time I was very near cars, when I'd "Thread the Needle" between two adjacent cars. Doing that already felt great and getting a "bonus" for it in the game felt great, and you can get combos of it. It took only a few minutes to get the initial logic in via prompts, but then it took LESS than a minute to say "hey not near, let's do between the cars", and was able to change it. Every feature I've added has been iterated on and polished, but some of the best features of my game are things I left OUT.

replies.author: 0bscuris
replies.body: Yeah, makes total sense. I have found the same, i try something, it changes the way i play but i’m not sure if it is good or bad yet until i layer one or more things on and then go, this whole path is no good and it’s cuz of that first mistake so it’s gotta go.
